findings.reason: The protected source is an expert-quality iterative preorder codec. Explicit null tokens make the grammar reversible, a right-before-left serialization stack preserves preorder, and parent-slot frames deserialize without recursion-depth risk. The local TreeNode and round-trip adapter satisfy the app contract cleanly, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 297 and its Python Codec design surface plus round-trip tree adapter. The Reference preserves the representation freedom and level-order clarification, both source examples without explanations, both constraints, and an accessible text equivalent of the source tree image.

The immutable native Codec remains tied to verified submission 2064355841. It and the protected app-local Codec have identical token grammar, iterative traversal, null handling, parent-slot reconstruction, and integer parsing; the local TreeNode definition and solve round trip are app-only adapters.

The legal 16/64/192-node left-skewed tiers span 12x, exercise every null marker and parent-slot transition, and stress repeated work on long remaining subtrees. The current source passes at +0.00 relative exponent and 0.98x largest ratio; a correct codec that recounts each remaining subtree before serialization passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +0.92 and 16.90x.

The Approach now defines node count n and height h, derives the exact 2n + 1 token count, separates total linear storage from O(h) stack depth, and explicitly covers empty trees plus signed and multi-digit token values.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving both examples without explanations, both constraints, the source-native clarification, and the informational equivalent of the sole source image.
